headline: High risk of prompt-injection, data leakage, and cascading errors when Kestra workflows feed Khoj’s retrieval/chat loop.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Kestra can ingest and emit workflow inputs, logs, messages, and files via stdin/stdout and shared storage, while Khoj reads indexed personal notes/files and supports chat/RAG. If Kestra-produced content is indexed or pasted into Khoj, attacker-controlled instructions can cross the boundary. The pathway is plausible but not proven by docs alone.
conditions: IF Kestra outputs are indexed into Khoj without provenance filtering
IF operators copy Kestra logs or artifacts into Khoj chat or notes
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to Kestra outputs before indexing
Exclude workflow logs from Khoj ingestion
Use a separate workspace for automation artifacts
Train operators to treat workflow text as untrusted
requires-engineering: enforce content-sanitization at the ingestion boundary

B_data_leakage.rationale: Kestra touches logs, database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications and has broad network egress; Khoj indexes personal notes/files and can use configured search providers or a cloud/self-hosted server. If both share a workspace or credentials, sensitive Kestra artifacts can be surfaced in Khoj and then transmitted onward. The blast radius includes secrets and personal data.
conditions: IF Kestra artifacts containing logs or database data are placed in Khoj-indexed folders
IF Khoj is configured to sync or search those folders
IF either agent is connected to third-party search or cloud endpoints
mitigations: Remove sensitive Kestra outputs from shared folders
Restrict Khoj indexing to a non-sensitive subdirectory
Rotate any secrets that may already be in logs
Disable external search providers for the shared corpus
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before indexing

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Kestra has filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and elevated-privilege requests; Khoj can read files and maintains shared index state across clients. They do not both write the same mutable resource by default, but if pointed at the same directory or index, Kestra can overwrite content that Khoj reads. The conflict is plausible and can corrupt shared artifacts.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to operate on the same filesystem path
IF Kestra writes artifacts into a directory Khoj indexes
IF multiple Khoj clients share the same index without locking
mitigations: Separate Kestra output and Khoj index directories
Make shared paths read-only for one side
Schedule non-overlapping runs
Back up the shared index before workflow execution
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Kestra can generate logs, artifacts, and notifications that Khoj may retrieve and present in chat. Khoj’s retrieval/chat model can treat indexed content as authoritative unless the operator verifies it. That creates a default pathway where automation output becomes conversational input, enabling mistaken downstream actions or false conclusions.
conditions: IF Khoj is used to summarize or act on Kestra-generated artifacts
IF operators rely on Khoj answers without checking the original workflow run
IF Kestra notifications are indexed as factual records
mitigations: Mark Kestra outputs as untrusted in the index
Require source-link review before acting on Khoj answers
Keep execution logs separate from knowledge notes
Use a checklist for any action derived from retrieved content
requires-engineering: add citation/verification gates in the workflow

E_compliance.rationale: Kestra handles workflow definitions, logs, database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications, while Khoj indexes personal notes/files and may use cloud or configured search providers. If regulated or personal data from Kestra is indexed into Khoj, retention and residency policies can diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated data from Kestra is copied into Khoj’s indexed corpus
IF Khoj is hosted or searched through a provider with different retention rules
IF deletion requests must propagate across both systems
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Khoj indexes
Document retention for both systems
Purge duplicated records on a fixed schedule
Verify where Khoj search providers store data
requires-engineering: implement synchronized deletion/export handling
